newsitem.title: USA: Pep Boys shrs crash, ratings driven down.
newsitem.headline: Pep Boys shrs crash, ratings driven down.

text.p: Shares of Pep Boys Manny Moe & Jack suffered a front-end collision Friday after the company released earnings significantly below Wall Street expectations.
Shares of the automotive service and parts retail chain fell 6-12/16 to 25-5/16 in afternoon trade on the New York Stock Exchange as analysts cut their ratings and lowered their earnings estimates.
"The company surprised people with their earnings and their statements about conditions in the market in California," said an industry analyst who asked not to be named.
On Thursday, after the market closed, Pep Boys reported second quarter earnings of $0.47 a share, compared to $0.49 a year earlier and a First Call consensus estimate of $0.56.
The company said weak do-it-youself demand hurt comparable store sales in California, which fell 2.9 percent. California accounts for about 23 percent of the chain's sales.
"This (sales trend) is a continuation of the trends witnessed in the first quarter, and it is unclear when it will reverse," William Julian, an analyst with Lehman Brothers, said in a report.
A spokesman for First Call told Reuters he was aware of seven analysts who had cut their ratings on Pep Boys, lowering the consenus rating to hold from buy.
He said the consensus earnings estimate for the fiscal year ending January 1998 had been reduced to $1.69 a share from $1.87, and the estiamte for the following year had been cut to $2.00 from $2.21.
